rows: A dry microburst occurred at the El Paso International Airport.
Very strong winds blew down power lines and unroofed several residences. Assistance was required by American Red Cross and the Fabens Volunteer Fire Department.

Golf ball size hail accumulated several inches, with strong winds blowing the hail into drifts more than 2 feet high. Driving was extremely hazardous on I-10, and crops suffered extensive damage. A funnel cloud was also observed.
An intense shaft of hail dropped nickel to quarter size hail over an area from the UTEP campus through downtown El Paso. Some automobiles received minor dents.
A few vehicles received dents and broken windshields in east central El Paso.
Several reports were received of golf ball size hail in Horizon City.
Horizon City got hit a second time overnight with large hail, this time ping pong ball size.

The third severe thunderstorm of the night dropped a great amount of quarter to half dollar size hail on far east El Paso. Unfortunately several car dealerships are located in this area and experienced damage to new vehicles. Hail sales were advertised for weeks to follow.
A porch was blown off a house and a tree was blown down.
Golfball hail fell briefly at one location in west El Paso.
Wind blew a 1 ton hangar door off its hinges. Two fences and a large tree was blown down near a main runway.
Several large signs were blown down in northeast El Paso.
Downburst winds estimated at 70 mph blew one tree over on a truck, while other fallen trees blocked streets in Fabens. Also, a roof was blown off a residence.
A gust of 61 mph was measured at a media mesonet.

A swath of large hail (quarter to hen's egg size) driven by 60 to 70 mph microburst winds caused extensive damage to a portion of west El Paso. Skylights were destroyed, roofs damaged, car windshields and south-facing house windows smashed. Dozens of automobiles suffered body dam…
The El Paso Fire Department reported power lines and trees down as well as a few roofs blown off from microburst winds estimated at 70 mph.
Wind-driven golfball size hail damaged many vehicles at auto dealerships and broke windows at residences.
A roof was blown off of a house in Horizon City.
Winds estimated at more than 60 mph downed numerous trees near Del Valle High School in El Paso's lower valley.
Hail, up to quarter size fell for 12 minutes.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell at Hueco Tanks State Park.
Golfball size hail fell south of Hueco Tanks State Park. This was the first of two supercells in El Paso County this day, but it remained over mainly a sparsely populated area.
Numerous skylights and automobiles were damaged from ping pong ball size hail.

Far east El Paso was hardest hit by this second supercell, with extensive golfball to possibly tennis ball size hail falling for 20 minutes. Thousands of automobiles were damaged, with several dealerships suffering much loss. Skylights were destroyed, roofs damaged and windows br…
The supercell continued southeastward and dropped golfball size hail on El Paso's lower valley area.
The supercell continued southeastward along I-10 for several miles. According to TxDOT, hundreds of vehicles along the interstate and other highways suffered extensive damage.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Horizon City by the Department of Public Safety.
A report was received of up to one inch diameter hail in Tornillo.
A peak gust of 58 mph was reported 3 miles northeast of El Paso.

Several severe wind reports were received across eastern and northeastern El Paso with a peak gust of 62 mph reported 3 miles north-northeast of El Paso. Other reports included 61 mph at Chapin High School and 60 mph at the El Paso International Airport.
A wind gust of 60 mph was estimated at the El Paso Texas Department of Transportation building.

Law enforcement reported 4 light poles blown down by high winds near mile marker 49 on Interstate 10. Extensive hail covered the ground and 0.49 inches of rain was reported in 20 minutes at Fabens Elementary School.
Penny sized hail was reported just near the intersection of Artcraft Road and Interstate 10.
Hail up to golf ball size was reported at the intersection of Interstate 10 and George Dieter.
Three-quarter inch hail was reported at Cielo Vista Mall.
One inch diameter hail was reported at the El Paso International Airport by contract observer.
Dime sized hail was reported at Horizon Blvd. and Interstate 10.
Large tree branches down along borderland road between Westside Drive and Doniphan.
A 61 mph gust was reported 6 miles north of Fort Bliss.
The El Paso ASOS recorded a peak gust of 78 mph with a wet microburst. In addition, a canopy at the gate entrance onto Fort Bliss collapsed due to the winds.
A 60 mph wind gust was reported near Montwood and Lee Trevino in East El Paso.
Trees and power lines were reported down in Canutillo from thunderstorm winds.
An estimated 60 mph wind gust was reported on the eastern slopes of the Franklin Mountains near Fort Bliss.
KFOX forwarded on a report of 1 inch hail in Vinton.
A spotter on the south side of the Franklin Mountains recorded a peak gust of 67 mph.
A peak gust of 64 mph was recorded by a NWS Employee just east of the Franklin Mountains in Northeast El Paso. Visibility was also near zero with blowing dust.
The ELP ASOS at El Paso International Airport reported a thunderstorm wind gust of 61 mph in association with a severe thunderstorm.
A trained spotter reported a 67 mph thunderstorm wind gust along with 1.12 inches of rain in 50 minutes as a severe thunderstorm moved past.
Mostly nickel sized hail with quarters mixed in.
Radio operators reported wind damage to several trees near San Elizario High School.
Reports of pea to quarter size hail on Interstate 10 at mile marker 41 northeast of Clint.
The El Paso Airport ASOS reported a peak gust of 62 mph.
Local media affiliate reported a 70mph wind gust at Ascarate Park.
Amateur radio operators reported power lines down along Desert Bloom St. in Montana Vista.

Broadcast media reported at least 50 large trees down in the Upper Valley near Sunset and Briarwood including some on power lines and a tree. Framing and boards on a new construction building near Sunland Park Drive and Constitution were completely blown down.
A spotter reported at least 70 mph winds near Artcraft and I-10. In addition half inch hail was also reported at same location.
Golf ball size hail reported by trucker on Interstate 10 via Twitter.
Hail damaged recently sprouted pecan trees.
Hail covered ground. Penny sized, but mostly smaller hail.
Public sent picture of hail covering ground at Executive and Rio Bravo.
The broadcast media reported damage to a billboard near Interstate 10 and Redd Road in West El Paso.
A peak wind gust of 59 mph was measured in West El Paso associated with outflow from thunderstorm near Chaparral.
Fort Bliss AWOS reported gust of 64 mph.
A 35 foot pine tree was blown down at intersection of Trawood and George Dieter.
Quarter sized hail near Canutillo High School.
Nickel sized hail was reported near Fort Bliss.
Near Kanozo Road in Horizon City.
Love's Truck Stop in Sparks off I-10.
Hail started accumulating on the ground.
Roof blown off mobile home and storage unit blown off the ground.
Penny size hail at Redd Rd and Resler.
Hail reported at Diana and US 54.
Hail covered the ground from US 54 and Diana to Sun Valley.
Measured by contract observers at the El Paso Airport.
Power lines down at Gateway and Hawkins.
Power lines down at Gateway and Yarbrough.
Trees down at Copia and Alameda.

Supercell thunderstorms (very rare for November in this area) affected much of El Paso. The strongest, which actually weakened before moving into the United States, produced golf ball hail over far east El Paso into Horizon City. This caused record breaking insurance claims for a…
Spotter 5 miles south-southwest of Hueco Tanks reported power out and pea size hail.
Dime size hail was reported just northwest of McNary.
There were several reports from the public near the Sunland Park Mall of hail up to quarter size that broke skylights and windows. Winds near 60 mph driving the hail intensified the effects.
Several trees down near the Sunland Park Mall.
Spotter measured a 62 mph gust in northeast El Paso.
A peak gust of 66 mph was recorded by an off duty NWS employee in northeast El Paso.
An 82 mph wind gust was recorded at the El Paso International Airport.
A spotter in northeast El Paso recorded a peak gust of 64 mph.
A photo was received of a weak landspout tornado near the town of Clint. No damage done.
Spotter reported dents to cars, windshields and house windows around the area of Buckley and North Stanton Streets.
Golf ball sized hail broke windshield around the UTEP area.
Observer reported one inch hail with some car damage.
Golf ball sized hail at Southwest University Park area.
A trained spotter recorded a 62 mph thunderstorm gust. Half inch hail and over an inch of rain were recorded with the storm.
A tree fell on a house in Canutillo.
A tree was downed and blocking a road just south of Canutillo.
Numerous reports of trees down and causing roads to be blocked across west El Paso.
Several reports of hail across west El Paso up to 1.25 inches in diameter. Sources included trained spotters, NWS Employee and public.
Hail up to one inch in diameter fell in Anthony which brought significant roof and vehicle damage to the area.
Time estimated from radar. Report received via Twitter.
Social Media report, time estimated based on radar.
Fabens Mesonet site reported a peak gust of 63 mph.
Tree of unknown size down in the street just south-southeast of Canutillo.
Emergency manager reported a tree in the street about 3 miles south-southeast of Canutillo.
Peak gust of 63 mph reported at the South Franklin Peak Mesonet site.
Public report of hail up to 1 inch in diameter.
Emergency Manager reported a tree had fallen on a power line near Fort Bliss.
Tree down at the intersection of Dyer and Haines Dr from Emergency Manager.
Trees were reported to have fallen on power lines in northeast El Paso.
Social media report showed hail up to the size of quarters near Fort Bliss.
The El Paso Airport ASOS recorded a peak gust of 73 mph.
Social media report of tree damage in northeast El Paso.
Report of a tree knocked down onto a trailer near Yarbrough and Alameda.
First responders reported power lines down on houses.
Social Media post of downed powerlines at Ft. Bliss.
The Fabens Mesonet station run by the Texas Water Development Board recorded a peak gust of 62 mph.
Outflow winds blew over a tree and pulled down a powerline leaving the area around the El Pavon Apartments without power.
